rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads harming one's own people as harming oneself, calling the general wording intended distributively a form of comprehensive expression.
rows.anchor: أشار ابن عطية وسماه اللف في القول ، أي الإجمال المراد به التوزيع

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf likens an affiliated person to oneself because kinship or shared religion makes them closely connected; this is close to the first explanation and treats the possessive pronouns figuratively.
rows.anchor: ذهب صاحب ( الكشاف ) إلى أنه من تشبيه الغير بالنفس لشدة اتصال الغير بالنفس في الأصل أو الدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reads the commands causatively: do not provoke another's killing and then suffer retaliation, or commit an offense that gets you expelled from your homes.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن المعنى لا تسفكون دماءكم بالتسبب في قتل الغير فيقتص منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage alludes to two Mosaic commandments among the Ten Commandments: do not kill and do not covet a neighbor's house.
rows.anchor: أشارت هذه الآية إلى وصيتين من الوصايا الإلاهية الواقعة في العهد المعروف بالكلمات العشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on coveting a neighbor's house blocks attempts to seize it by implication, as a preventative legal measure.
rows.anchor: فإن النهي عن شهوة بيت القريب لقصد سد ذريعة السعي في اغتصابه منه بفحوى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is attributed to the addressees because, as followers of Torah, they had committed themselves to all its contents.
rows.anchor: إضافة ( ميثاق ) إلى ضمير المخاطبين مراعى فيها أنهم لما كانوا متدينين بشريعة التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb taqtulūna can be a circumstantial clause or predicate; its imperfect form, like tukh’rijūna, marks repeated conduct as their characteristic practice.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { تقتلون } حال أو خبر . وعبر بالمضارع لقصد الدلالة على التجدد وأن ذلك من شأنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt gives an unattributed poetic line and cites al-Nābigha as an unusual further example of the construction under discussion, with hāʾ in each line.
rows.anchor: وشذ بغير ذلك نحو قول النابغة : ها إن تاعذرة إن لا تكن نفعت

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf makes all the addressees forebears, treating the apparent shift at thumma antum hāʾulāʾ as a figurative change in the same audience's attributes; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this forced and unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وجعل في ( الكشاف ) المقصود بالخطابات كلها في هذه الآية مرادا به أسلاف الحاضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The historical target is most likely the Jewish tribes of Qurayẓa, Naḍīr, and Qaynuqāʿ, especially their conduct in the wars of Buʿāth between Aws and Khazraj.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن المقصود يهود قريظة والنضير وقينقاع . وأراد من ذلك بخاصة ما حدث بينهم في حروب بعاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During a long period of neutrality, the Jews considered joining the losing Aws; Khazraj threatened them, and the Jews declined alliance with either side before handing over forty Qurayẓa and Naḍīr boys as hostages to Khazraj.
rows.anchor: اعتزل اليهود الفريقين زمنا طويلا والأوس مغلوبون في سائر أيام القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khazraji ʿAmr ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Bayāḍī urged his people to take the Jews' attractive lands and palms, threatening to kill the hostages unless Qurayẓa and Naḍīr surrendered their homes; Kaʿb ibn Asad advised defending the homes even if the boys died.
rows.anchor: ثم إن عمرو بن النعمان البياضي الخزرجي أطمع قومه أن يتحولوا لقريظة والنضير لحسن أرضهم ونخلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Qurayẓa and Naḍīr refused, ʿAmr killed the hostages; they allied with Aws, Khazraj allied with Qaynuqāʿ, and Jews fought at Buʿāth five years before the Hijra, expelling or capturing the defeated.
rows.anchor: فلما أجابت قريظة والنضير عمرا بأنهم يمنعون ديارهم عدا عمرو على الغلمان فقتلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterward, Jews raised money to ransom Jewish captives held by their Aws or Khazraj allies. When Arabs censured this contradiction, they said fighting was forbidden but they were ashamed to abandon allies and had been commanded to ransom captives.
rows.anchor: فعيرت العرب اليهود بذلك وقالت : كيف تقاتلونهم ثم تفدونهم بأموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is an accusing reproach: they fought their fellow Jews against Torah but followed it to ransom captives; calling selective obedience belief and rejection disbelief vilifies them and warns that deliberate violation can lead to disbelief.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري توبيخي أي كيف تعمدتم مخالفة التوراة في قتال إخوانكم واتبعتموها في فداء أسراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting belief under reproach marks the combination as astonishing: they nearly, or perhaps actually, denied the ban on expelling fellow Jews; denial of a decisive religious rule takes one out of the religion.
rows.anchor: وإنما وقع { تؤمنون } في حيز الإنكار تنبيها على أن الجمع بين الأمرين عجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ may connect the question to taqtulūna anfusakum and its coordinated material, or to an elided clause indicated by the question; the syntax is revisited at 2:87.
rows.anchor: والفاء عاطفة على { تقتلون أنفسكم } ، وما عطف عليه ، عطفت الاستفهام أو عطفت مقدرا

words: فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in famā jazāʾ may connect to an omitted premise implied by the reproach, or directly to the reproachful question.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم } فصيحة عاطفة على محذوف دل عليه الاستفهام الإنكاري

words: فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم
rows.speaker: عبد الحكيم
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm calls the clause parenthetical, with fāʾ introducing the parenthesis.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الحكيم : إن الجملة معترضة والاعتراض بالفاء

words: فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم
rows.speaker: عبد الحكيم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm's parenthesis analysis: a concluding parenthesis should summarize rather than add a ruling, and classical parentheticals are not ordinarily introduced by a particle other than wāw.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد معنى ولفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khizyun is sudden humiliation of the self from insult, disgrace, or domination; the noun names the resulting state, while its verb follows samiʿa and its verbal noun has fatḥa on khāʾ.
rows.anchor: والخزي بالكسر ذل في النفس طارىء عليها فجأة لإهانة لحقتها أو معرة صدرت منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliation refers to later Jewish defeats and subjugation: Naḍīr's expulsion, Qurayẓa's killing, the conquest of Khaybar, and their abasement among nations.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخزي ما لحق باليهود بعدتلك الحروب من المذلة بإجلاء النضير عن ديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read yaruddūna with third-person yāʾ; ʿĀṣim, in one transmission, reads taruddūna with second-person tāʾ, guided by the sense of man and the following minkum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( يردون ) و ( يعملون ) بياء الغيبة ، وقرأ عاصم في رواية عنه ( تردون ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For yaʿmalūna, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Yaʿqūb read the third-person yāʾ; the passage says the majority read second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير ويعقوب : ( يعملون ) بياء الغيبة وقرأه الجمهور بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that God punishes those who deviate from the path with punishments in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقد دلت هذه الآية على أن الله يعاقب الحائدين عن الطريق بعقوبات في الدنيا وعقوبات في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative phrase functions as it does in 2:5, while buying worldly life for the afterlife parallels buying misguidance for guidance in 2:16.
rows.anchor: وقد وقع اسم الإشارة وهو قوله : { أولئك الذين اشتروا } موقع نظيره في قوله : { أولئك على هدى من ربهم }

words: فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending resembles 2:48, which likewise says that intercession or ransom is unavailable and that they receive no help.
rows.anchor: والقول في { فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون } قريب من القول في { ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks consequence: so grave a crime warrants severe punishment, with no helper to avert or lighten it.
rows.anchor: وموقع الفاء في قوله : { فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب } هو الترتب لأن المجرم بمثل هذا الجرم العظيم يناسبه العذاب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is coordinated to 2:89 through 2:88, or may be treated as coordinated directly to 2:88 by the usual rule for linking to an already coordinated clause.
rows.anchor: معطوف على قوله : { ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله } ( البقرة : 89 ) المعطوف على قوله : { وقالوا قلوبنا غلف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses recount successive excuses for rejecting Islam: they claimed sealed hearts, rejected the long-awaited scripture from envy, then claimed belief only in what God revealed to Moses; the polemic leads into 2:106.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله من عطف حكايات أحوالهم في معاذيرهم عن الإعراض عن الدعوة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply is self-exculpation: they imply they already possess the virtue of believing God's revelation and may be content with the Torah, avoiding the shame of a bare refusal to believe the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أرادوا به الاعتذار وتعلة أنفسهم لأنهم لما قيل لهم { آمنوا بما أنزل الله } علموا أنهم إن امتنعوا امتناعا مجردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect nuʾmin suggests continued adherence to their own scripture; in response to a call intended to include the Qur'an, it implies that they believe only what was revealed to them and treat belief in another revelation as denying theirs.
rows.anchor: وهذا وجه التعبير في الحكاية عنهم بلفظ المضارع { نؤمن } أي ندوم على الإيمان بما أنزل علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews defended exclusive belief in Mosaic revelation by claiming their law could not be abrogated; they accused Muhammad's law of invalidating Torah and invoked badāʾ, as if God learned belatedly what to legislate.
rows.anchor: وهم في عذرهم ذلك يدعون أن شريعتهم لا تنسخ ويقولون إن محمدا وصف التوراة بأنها حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had already exposed their lack of fidelity to their own law and their envy of the Qur'an; the present passage now dismantles their argument against abrogation.
rows.anchor: وقد قدمنا أن الله تعالى رد عليهم عذرهم وفضحهم بأنهم ليسوا متمسكين بشرعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary purpose is to teach Muslims that a later law may replace an earlier law and that a ruling within one law may replace an earlier ruling; the direct address to Muslims also refutes the Jews implicitly.
rows.anchor: والمقصد الأصلي من هذا هو تعليم المسلمين أصلا من أصول الشرائع وهو أصل النسخ الذي يطرأ على شريعة بشريعة بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word āya can conventionally denote a message, naming something by its customary associate; the cited verse uses āya in that sense.
rows.anchor: ألكني إليها عمرك الله يا فتى بآية ما جاءت إلينا تهاديا ولذا أيضا سموا الرسالة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here āya means its legal ruling, whether the wording is removed or retained, because the verse explains why rulings are repealed rather than why Qur'anic wording disappears.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالآية هنا حكم الآية سواء أزيل لفظها أم أبقى لفظها لأن المقصود بيان حكمة إبطال الأحكام

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines naskh as removing one thing by another thing that takes its place.
rows.anchor: والنسخ إزالة الشي بشيء آخر قاله الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic verb can depict removal and replacement, as sunlight removes shade or shade displaces sunlight, and as bees move wax and honey to another cell.
rows.anchor: تقول نسخت الشمس الظل لأن شعاعها أزال الظل وخلفه في موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naskh may mean removal alone, as when wind erases a trace, or the special establishing of a remover; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects a sense of mere establishment.
rows.anchor: وقد يطلق على الإزالة فقط دون تعويض كقولهم نسخت الريح الأثر وعلى الإثبات لكن على إثبات خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the transcription of a book naskh is figurative imitation of moving its letters to a new page, not proof that naskh means mere establishment; calling a child his father's copy is metaphor upon metaphor.
rows.anchor: لكن هذا توهم لأن إطلاق النسخ على محاكاة حروف الكتاب إطلاق مجازي بالصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naskh does not mean simple disappearance without removal: night does not abrogate day, since night is original darkness from the absence of an illuminating body.
rows.anchor: ولا يطلق النسخ على الزوال بدون إزالة فلا تقول نسخ الليل النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse naskh is removal with a replacement, as shown by the following promise; legal theorists define it as lifting a legal ruling by a later revealed address.
rows.anchor: والمراد من النسخ هنا الإزالة وإثبات العوض بدليل قوله : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definition excludes newly introduced legislation, which lifts nothing, and the end of original permissibility, since that is absence of obligation before revelation rather than a legal ruling; scripture specifies permissions only in special contexts.
rows.anchor: فخرج التشريع المستأنف إذ ليس برفع ، وخرج بقولنا الحكم الشرعي رفع البراءة الأصلية بالشرع المستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is the conditional's answer; its form pairs each kind of abrogation, forgetfulness, or deferral with a suitable replacement or provision at the corresponding time.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها } جواب الشرط وجعله جوابا مشعر بأن هذين الحالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With abrogation, what comes is the superseding law or ruling; with causing forgetfulness, it may be a superseding rule or a later contrary rule; with deferral, other rules sustain people during the delay.
rows.anchor: فالمأتي به مع النسخ هو الناسخ من شريعة أو حكم والمأتي به مع الإنساء من النسيان هو الناسخ أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Goodness may mean serving human interests, averting harm, bringing good outcomes or reward, or easing hardship; a stricter rule can still better serve the interest. Each case has either benefit or equivalence, and aw allows either and possibly both.
rows.anchor: وقد أجملت جهة الخيرية والمثلية لتذهب نفس السامع كل مذهب ممكن فتجده مرادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include Islam replacing Torah and Gospel with a better law, and the law of Ṣāliḥ replacing Hūd's with an equivalent one, since each benefits its community in a comparable way.
rows.anchor: نسخ شريعة مع الإتيان بخير منها كنسخ التوراة والإنجيل بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A better ruling example is the initial censure or disfavor of wine in 2:219, later replaced by its categorical prohibition: better for public interest though less lenient.
rows.anchor: مثل نسخ كراهة الخمر الثابتة بقوله : { قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rule can also be better through greater leniency: permission for food, drink, and marital relations at night in Ramadan replaced the earlier restriction after sleep.
rows.anchor: كنسخ تحريم الأكل والشرب وقربان النساء في ليل رمضان بعد وقت الإفطار عند الغروب إذا نام الصائم قبل أن يتعشى

rows.speaker: صحيح البخاري
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī says Muslims rejoiced when the nighttime Ramadan permission was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال في الحديث في ( صحيح البخاري ) ففرح المسلمون بنزولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An example of a law fading away is the law of Adam and Noah giving way to Moses's better, broader law; Idrīs's law is offered as equivalent to Noah's.
rows.anchor: نسيان شريعة بمعنى اضمحلالها كشريعة آدم ونوح مع مجيء شريعة موسى وهي أفضل وأوسع وشريعة إدريس مثلا وهي مثل شريعة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruling example is ten known sucklings being replaced by five, then both forgotten, with 4:23 retaining the general rule of milk kinship; the outcomes are equivalent and the small difference poses no hardship.
rows.anchor: كان فيما نزل عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن فنسخن بخمس معلومات ثم نسيا معا وجاءت آية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes nisyān to mean abandoning a ruling; on that reading its meaning and cases collapse into those of deferral or causing forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد من النسيان الترك وهو حينئذ يرجع معناه وصوره إلى معنى وصور الإنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise shows that changing or delaying laws does not compromise God's knowledge, wisdom, or lordship: each change suits people's conditions, advances their interests mercifully, and preserves worldly order until the final law.
rows.anchor: والمقصد من قوله تعالى : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها } إظهار منتهى الحكمة والرد عليهم بأنهم لا يهمهم أن تنسخ شريعة بشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same divine purpose culminates in Islam as the final religion and in the religion prescribed to Muhammad as the one previously enjoined on Noah.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال : { إن الدين عند الله الإسلام } ( آل عمران : 19 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Better or equivalent applies to both abrogation and forgetfulness or deferral, not as a fold-and-unfold distribution; each case is compensation or reinforcement, so people are never left without provision and no divine change of mind is implied.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الإتيان بخير أو بمثل راجع إلى كل من النسخ والإنساء فيكون الإتيان بخير من المنسوخة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes understand nunsihā as God making Muslims forget a verse or surah, or making the Prophet forget it, so that collective loss would indicate abrogation.
rows.anchor: ما قاله بعض المفسرين في قوله تعالى : { ننسها } أنه إنساء الله تعالى المسلمين للآية أو للسورة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports through al-Ṭabarānī that two men forgot a surah the Prophet had taught them; he told them it was among what had been abrogated and forgotten and to leave it.
rows.anchor: بسنده إلى ابن عمر قال ( قرأ رجلان سورة أقرأهما إياها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr grades the Ibn ʿUmar report weak because its chain includes Sulaymān ibn Arqam.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير هذا الحديث في سنده سليمان بن أرقم وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the report munkar and questions how a report so unusual could have escaped the leading hadith scholars.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية هذا حديث منكر أغرب به الطبراني وكيف خفي مثله على أئمة الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the claim that mass forgetfulness proves abrogation; a Prophet's forgetting a passage God intended to remove rather than preserve as Qur'an is possible in principle, but did not occur.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن نسيان النبيء ما أراد الله نسخه ولم يرد أن يثبته قرآنا جائز ، أي لكنه لم يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is protected from ordinary forgetfulness before delivering revelation; after delivery and its preservation by Muslims, such a lapse is possible.
rows.anchor: فأما النسيان الذي هو آفة في البشر فالنبيء معصوم عنه قبل التبليغ ، وأما بعد التبليغ وحفظ المسلمين له فجائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse during prayer; after prayer Ubayy asked why he had not reminded him, thinking it had been lifted, and the Prophet replied that he had forgotten it.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه أسقط آية من سورة في الصلاة فلما فرغ قال لأبي لم لم تذكرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Temporary forgetfulness followed by recollection is possible but is not the verse's meaning, since that conflicts with its promise of a replacement; permanent loss of Qur'an is likely impermissible.
rows.anchor: والحق عندي أن النسيان العارض الذي يتذكر بعده جائز ولا تحمل عليه الآية لمنافاته لظاهر قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise in 87:6 that the Prophet will not forget supports the impossibility of permanent Qur'anic loss; 87:7's exception is an accommodation in the promise, to be explained in Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } ( الأعلى : 6 ) دليل عليه وقوله : { إلا ما شاء الله }

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that Muslims once recited a surah nearly as long as Barāʾa, then forgot it except for a saying about Adam's desire for more wealth and God's acceptance of repentance; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the report strange.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ورد في ( صحيح مسلم ) عن أنس قال : كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها في الطول ببراءة فانسيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets Anas's report as a surah whose recitation and rulings had both been abrogated; Muslims' forgetting wording removed from Qur'an is unsurprising.
rows.anchor: وتأويله أن هنالك سورة نسخت قراءتها وأحكامها ، ونسيان المسلمين لما نسخ لفظه من القرآن غير عجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the prayer, min dhurriyyatinā and ummatan muslimatan are coordinated objects governed by wajʿalnā; min is partitive.
rows.anchor: يتعين أن يكون { من ذريتنا } و { مسلمة } معمولين لفعل { واجعلنا } بطريق العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks that their religion endure among some descendants, balancing concern for their offspring's virtue with proper etiquette in supplication.
rows.anchor: وهذا دعاء ببقاء دينهما في ذريتهما ، و ( من ) في قوله : { ومن ذريتنا } للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim knew his descendants would form many nations and that worldly wisdom leaves both good and evil among them, so he asked for what is ordinarily possible rather than every descendant's virtue.
rows.anchor: لأن نبوءة إبراهيم تقتضي علمه بأنه ستكون ذريته أمما كثيرة وأن حكمة الله في هذا العالم جرت على أنه لا يخلو من اشتماله على الأخيار والأشرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this point the passage begins indirectly addressing polytheists who abandoned monotheism, while preparing to establish the honor of the Muhammadan religion.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا ابتدىء التعريض بالمشركين الذين أعرضوا عن التوحيد واتبعوا الشرك ، والتمهيد لشرف الدين المحمدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah has many senses; here it means a sizable community united by an important bond such as lineage, religion, or time, as in the community of Muhammad gathered by belief in his prophethood.
rows.anchor: والأمة اسم مشترك يطلق على معان كثيرة والمراد منها هنا الجماعة العظيمة التي يجمعها جامع له بال من نسب أو دين أو زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun follows the fuʿla pattern, which can mark a passive result; Ibn ʿĀshūr derives it from al-amm, intending, because different groups orient toward the encompassing community.
rows.anchor: وهي بزنة فعله وهذه الزنة تدل على المفعول مثل لقطة وضحكة وقدوة ، فالأمة بمعنى مأمومة اشتقت من الأم بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:38, animals being communities like humans is a vivid comparison: reflection on their exact creation and ordered lives reveals communities like ours, a point people had overlooked.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : { وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim's prayer was fulfilled among the Arabs who embraced Islam before and after the Hijra; the small number of exceptions did not break the community, and the next prayer signals this fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وقد استجيبت دعوة إبراهيم في المسلمين من العرب الذين تلاحقوا بالإسلام قبل الهجرة وبعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Israelites also converted, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, but their number did not cohere into a community of nation-sized scale.
rows.anchor: وأما من أسلموا من بني إسرائيل مثل عبد الله بن سلام فلم يلتئم منهم عدد أمة
